mainTopic: מנשה and the value of suffering, אבא שאול on saying ה׳'s Name, and how ירבעם's arrogance led him to the golden calves and cost him עולם הבא.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי עקיבא's proof that suffering is precious. חזקיה taught Torah to the whole world and surely taught his son מנשה, yet only suffering brought מנשה back to ה׳. A ברייתא then lists three who came to ה׳ with a demand: קין, עשו and מנשה. The גמרא returns to the משנה and explains אבא שאול's ruling: one who says ה׳'s Name as written, outside the מקדש and in casual speech, loses עולם הבא. Next it turns to the kings who lose עולם הבא, starting with ירבעם. It explains his name and his father נבט's names, and lists three who 'looked but did not see': נבט, אחיתופל and פרעה's astrologers. A פסוק proves ירבעם loses עולם הבא. רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן explain how he rose by rebuking שלמה and fell through public disrespect and arrogance. Fearing he would look like רחבעם's servant in the עזרה, ירבעם made two golden calves. He tricked the elders into agreeing by seating a wicked man next to each righteous one.

steps.title: A verse showing that חזקיה spread Torah widely
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in משלי shows that חזקיה's men copied and spread Torah wisdom, so חזקיה was a great Torah teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: "These too are the proverbs of שלמה, which the men of חזקיה, king of יהודה, copied."
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing רבי עקיבא's proof, the גמרא quotes a פסוק showing that חזקיה spread Torah to many people. This is setting up the next move, a question about his son מנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חזקיה's people were copying and spreading שלמה's wisdom, then חזקיה was a teacher of Torah for the whole nation. That fact will be used to show that מנשה surely got a great Torah education from his father.

keyTerms.meaning: The proverbs of King שלמה (the book of משלי)
חזקיה, the righteous king of יהודה and father of מנשה

phrases.english: "These too are the proverbs of Solomon
which the men of Hezekiah copied,
king of Judah."

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּם אֵלֶּה מִשְׁלֵי שְׁלֹמֹה אֲשֶׁר הֶעְתִּיקוּ אַנְשֵׁי חִזְקִיָּה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's derivation from the previous section about מנשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה spread Torah to the masses.

steps.title: Would חזקיה teach the world but not his own son?
steps.stepSummary: A pointed question: it makes no sense that חזקיה taught everyone Torah except his own son מנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible that חזקיה king of יהודה taught Torah to the whole world, and did not teach Torah to his son מנשה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a rhetorical question. Since חזקיה taught everyone, he obviously taught מנשה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not really a doubt. It proves that מנשה had the best possible Torah teacher. That makes his turning bad, and later turning back, even more striking.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible that...? (opens a rhetorical question)
מנשה, the wicked son of חזקיה who later did תשובה

phrases.english: And is it possible that Hezekiah, king of Judah,
taught Torah to the entire world,
and to Menashe his son he did not teach Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי חִזְקִיָּה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה לְכׇל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לִימֵּד תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק from step 1 to raise a rhetorical question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that מנשה lacked Torah teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A father who taught the whole world would surely have taught his own son.

steps.title: Only suffering turned מנשה around
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה worked hard teaching מנשה, but none of it helped. Only יסורין (suffering) brought him back, as the פסוק in דברי הימים describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, with all the effort and toil he put into him, nothing brought him to the good except suffering. As it says: "ה׳ spoke to מנשה and his people, but they did not listen. So ה׳ brought upon them the army commanders of the king of אשור, who captured מנשה with hooks, bound him in copper chains, and led him to בבל."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חזקיה did teach מנשה, with great effort, but it didn't work. Only suffering, being captured and taken to Babylon, changed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the key point. Teaching and words failed, since 'they did not listen.' Then suffering came. The next step will show that this suffering is what brought מנשה back.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought him up to the good path

phrases.english: Rather, from all the effort that he exerted on him
and from all the toil that he toiled over him,
nothing brought him up to the good except suffering,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְדַבֵּר ה׳ אֶל מְנַשֶּׁה וְאֶל עַמּוֹ
phrases.english: as it is stated: "And ה׳ spoke to Menashe and to his people
but they did not listen.

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּבֵא ה׳ עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת שָׂרֵי הַצָּבָא
phrases.english: And ה׳ brought upon them the army commanders
of the king of Assyria,
and they captured Menashe with hooks
and bound him in copper chains and led him to Babylon."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִכׇּל טוֹרַח שֶׁטָּרַח בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rhetorical question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the teaching happened but failed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe מנשה went bad because he was never taught.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was taught well, but only suffering changed him.

steps.title: In his distress מנשה prayed and was answered
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוקים show that once מנשה was suffering, he humbled himself, prayed, and was brought back. Then he recognized ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "When he was in distress, he pleaded before ה׳ his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers. He prayed to Him, and He accepted him, heard his plea, and brought him back to ירושלים to his kingdom. Then מנשה knew that ה׳ is God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוקים to show what the suffering led to: מנשה humbled himself, prayed, and came to know ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'when he was in distress' tie his תשובה directly to the suffering. This completes the proof that suffering, and not teaching, is what brought him back.

keyTerms.meaning: And when he was in distress

phrases.english: And it is written: "And when he was in distress,
he pleaded before ה׳ his God
and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
And he prayed to Him, and He accepted his plea
and heard his supplication
and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom,

phrases.aramaic: וַיֵּדַע מְנַשֶּׁה כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים״.
phrases.english: and Menashe knew that ה׳ is God."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: וּכְהָצֵר לוֹ חִלָּה אֶת פְּנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 3 by showing the result of the suffering.
steps.raayaObject: That suffering is what brought מנשה to תשובה

steps.title: Conclusion: suffering is precious
steps.stepSummary: From מנשה's story we learn that יסורין are precious.
steps.simpleTranslation: So you have learned that suffering is precious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion of רבי עקיבא's proof: suffering is precious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suffering did what years of a great father's teaching could not do. It brought a very wicked person back to ה׳, so it is something precious.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה taught מנשה Torah with great effort, but only suffering brought מנשה back. That is why רבי עקיבא says יסורין are precious.

phrases.english: So you have learned that suffering is precious.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁחֲבִיבִין יִסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the proof in steps 3–4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Suffering is precious because it can bring a person back to ה׳.

steps.title: Three who came with a demand, starting with קין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three people who came to ה׳ with a demand: קין, עשו and מנשה. קין argued that his sin was not too big to be forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Three came with a demand: קין, עשו and מנשה. קין, as it is written: "Is my sin too great to bear?" He said before Him: Master of the World, is my sin greater than that of the six hundred thousand who will sin before You, whom You will forgive?
steps.whatsHappening: Since we were talking about מנשה, the גמרא brings a ברייתא listing three people who came to ה׳ with a demand. It starts with קין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קין's words 'גדול עוני מנשוא' are read as a question rather than a confession. He is asking whether his sin is really too big to forgive. His argument is that ה׳ will forgive a whole nation for a sin, so He should forgive him too.

keyTerms.meaning: With a demand, a pressing claim

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Three came with a demand,
and these are they: Cain, Esau and Menashe.
Cain, as it is written: "Is my sin too great to bear?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:13. Here קין's words are read as a question, not a confession.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
is my sin any greater than that of the six hundred thousand
who are destined to sin before You
and You forgive them?
phrases.notes: The six hundred thousand are the Jewish people in the desert, who will sin and still be forgiven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה בָּאוּ בַּעֲלִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by the theme of מנשה's turning to ה׳.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קין, עשו and מנשה each came to ה׳ with a demand. קין's demand was to be forgiven.

steps.title: עשו's demand for a blessing
steps.stepSummary: עשו's demand was his cry to his father: 'Do you have only one blessing?'
steps.simpleTranslation: עשו, as it is written: "Do you have only one blessing, my father?"
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second example. עשו pressed יצחק for a blessing of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשו did not accept that the blessing was gone. He demanded that his father find another one for him.

phrases.aramaic: עֵשָׂו, דִּכְתִיב: ״הַבְרָכָה אַחַת הִיא לָךְ אָבִי״.
phrases.english: Esau, as it is written: "Do you have only one blessing, my father?"

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵשָׂו, דִּכְתִיב: הַבְרָכָה אַחַת הִיא לָךְ אָבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עשו demanded a blessing of his own.

steps.title: מנשה's demand: calling to ה׳ last
steps.stepSummary: מנשה first called out to many idols. Only in the end did he call to the God of his fathers.
steps.simpleTranslation: מנשה: at first he called out to many gods, and in the end he called out to the God of his fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the third example, מנשה. He tried every idol first and turned to ה׳ only at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His prayer counts as a 'demand' because he turned to ה׳ only after everything else failed, as a kind of test. Even so, as step 4 showed, ה׳ answered him.

phrases.english: Menashe: at first he called out to many gods,
and in the end he called out to the God of his fathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנַשֶּׁה – בַּתְּחִילָּה קָרָא לֶאֱלוֹהוֹת הַרְבֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and last item in the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנשה turned to ה׳ only after trying all the idols.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: אבא שאול on saying ה׳'s Name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where אבא שאול adds to the list of those who lose עולם הבא: one who pronounces ה׳'s Name as it is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: Also one who pronounces the Name with its letters, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes אבא שאול's addition. This sets up the next step, which explains exactly what case he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists people who have no share in עולם הבא. אבא שאול adds a person who says the special Name of ה׳ the way it is spelled, letter by letter.

keyTerms.meaning: One who pronounces the Name (of ה׳)
With its letters, as it is written

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַהוֹגֶה אֶת הַשֵּׁם בְּאוֹתִיּוֹתָיו וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Also one who pronounces the Name with its letters, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: he too has no share in עולם הבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף הַהוֹגֶה אֶת הַשֵּׁם בְּאוֹתִיּוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who pronounces ה׳'s Name as written has no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: When saying the Name is so serious
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that אבא שאול means saying the Name outside the מקדש, in casual speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And this is in the outlying areas, and in casual speech.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains the exact case behind אבא שאול's ruling. It means someone saying the Name outside the מקדש, in a casual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the Name is not always forbidden, since it was said in the מקדש. The punishment is for someone who says it outside, for no proper purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: אבא שאול does not mean that saying the Name is forbidden everywhere. The ברייתא limits it to outside the מקדש and in a casual way.

phrases.english: It was taught: And this is in the outlying areas,
phrases.notes: He means anywhere outside the מקדש, where the Name was said properly.

phrases.english: and in casual speech.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: וּבַגְּבוּלִין, וּבִלְשׁוֹן עָגָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case of אבא שאול's ruling from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling applies to saying the Name outside the מקדש, in casual speech.

steps.title: What the names ירבעם and בן נבט mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about three kings and four commoners. A ברייתא explains the name ירבעם in three ways and explains 'בן נבט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: three kings and four commoners lose עולם הבא. The Rabbis taught: ירבעם means he debased the people. Another explanation: he made strife among the people. Another explanation: he made strife between the Jewish people and their Father in Heaven. 'בן נבט' means a son who looked but did not see.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the משנה, the list of kings and commoners. It starts with the first king, ירבעם, and explains what his name hints at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the name ירבעם as a hint to the harm he did: lowering the people, splitting the people, and pulling the people away from ה׳. Each explanation is worse than the one before. 'נבט' is read as 'looked', meaning someone who looked but got it wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Commoners, regular people who were not kings
Looked but did not see; he saw something and misunderstood it

phrases.english: Three kings and four commoners, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
Yorovam: because he debased the people.
phrases.notes: It's a play on sounds: ירבעם sounds like ריבע עם.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
Yorovam: because he made strife among the people.
Another explanation:
Yorovam: because he made strife
between the Jewish people and their Father in Heaven.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן נְבָט – בֵּן שֶׁנִּיבַּט וְלֹא רָאָה.
phrases.english: Son of Nebat: a son who looked but did not see.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מְלָכִים וְאַרְבָּעָה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing אבא שאול's addition, the גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name ירבעם hints at how he harmed the people, and 'בן נבט' hints at someone who looked but misunderstood.

steps.title: נבט, מיכה and שבע בן בכרי are one person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that נבט, מיכה and שבע בן בכרי are three names for one man, and explains the first two names.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: He is נבט, he is מיכה, he is שבע בן בכרי. נבט, because he looked but did not see. מיכה, because he was crushed in a building. And what is his real name? His name is שבע בן בכרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying that ירבעם's father had three names. It explains two of them as nicknames and says the third is his real name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only שבע בן בכרי is his actual name. נבט and מיכה are descriptions: נבט for looking and misunderstanding, מיכה for being crushed in a building. This links the father of ירבעם to other people mentioned in the תנ״ך.

phrases.english: It was taught:
He is Nebat, he is Micah,
he is Sheba son of Bichri.
Nebat: because he looked but did not see.
Micah: because he was crushed in a building.
phrases.notes: Another sound play: מיכה sounds like נתמכמך, 'squashed down'.

phrases.english: And what is his real name?
His name is Sheba son of Bichri.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא: הוּא נְבָט, הוּא מִיכָה, הוּא שֶׁבַע בֶּן בִּכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the name נבט from the previous step and adds that he had two other names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבט and מיכה are nicknames; the man's real name was שבע בן בכרי.

steps.title: Three who looked but did not see
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three who saw a sign but misunderstood it: נבט, אחיתופל and the astrologers of פרעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Three looked but did not see, and these are they: נבט, אחיתופל, and the astrologers of פרעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a list of three who 'looked but did not see.' It is setting up the next step, which explains what נבט saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'looked but did not see' now becomes a group of people. Each one saw a real sign about the future but drew the wrong conclusion from it.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's advisor who joined אבשלום's rebellion
Astrologers, people who read the stars
And these are they; opens a list

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three looked but did not see,
and these are they:
Nebat, and Ahithophel, and the astrologers of Pharaoh.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה נִיבְּטוּ וְלֹא רָאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the phrase 'looked but did not see' used for נבט and shows that two others share it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבט, אחיתופל and פרעה's astrologers all saw a true sign and misread it.

steps.title: What נבט saw and how he misread it
steps.stepSummary: נבט saw fire coming out of his body and thought he would become king. In truth, it meant his son ירבעם would come out of him and rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: נבט saw fire coming out of his private part. He thought it meant he would be king, but that was not so. It was ירבעם who came out of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first name on the list: what exactly נבט saw and why it counts as 'looking but not seeing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign was true: kingship was coming from נבט. His mistake was thinking it meant himself. The fire came from the place children come from, so it pointed to a son, ירבעם, who did become king.

keyTerms.meaning: Came out of him, was born from him

steps.whatToRemember: 'Looked but did not see' means seeing a true sign and misunderstanding it. נבט's sign was about his son ירבעם, not about himself.

phrases.english: Nebat saw fire coming out of his private part.
He thought that he himself would rule,
but that was not so.
It was Jeroboam who came out of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְבָט רָאָה אֵשׁ שֶׁיּוֹצֵאת מֵאַמָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first person on the list from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבט saw a true sign of kingship, but it was about his son ירבעם, not about him.

steps.title: אחיתופל's misread sign
steps.stepSummary: אחיתופל saw a sign of royalty and thought he would be king. In truth, it meant that שלמה המלך would come from his granddaughter בת שבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחיתופל saw צרעת shining on his body and thought he would be king. He was wrong. It meant that שלמה would come from בת שבע, his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second person on the list of those who misread a sign: אחיתופל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as נבט in the last step. The sign was real, but it pointed to a descendant, not to the man himself. אחיתופל thought he would rule, but the king came from בת שבע.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's adviser, who later joined אבשלום's rebellion
A skin affliction, here seen as a shining sign
But it is not so; that was a mistake

phrases.english: Ahithophel saw leprosy
that shone on his private part.
He thought that he himself would rule,
but it is not so.
Bathsheba his daughter,
phrases.notes: She was really his son's daughter. A granddaughter can be called a daughter.

phrases.english: it was from her that Solomon came out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחִיתוֹפֶל רָאָה צָרַעַת שֶׁזָּרְחָה לוֹ עַל אַמָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item on the list from step 13, following the pattern set by נבט in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחיתופל's sign pointed to שלמה, his descendant through בת שבע, and not to his own kingship.

steps.title: פרעה's astrologers and מי מריבה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains that פרעה's astrologers saw that Israel's savior would be struck through water. So פרעה ordered the baby boys thrown into the river. They did not realize it meant משה's punishment at מי מריבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: פרעה's astrologers misread a sign, as רבי חמא ברבי חנינא taught. The פסוק says 'These are the waters of מריבה,' meaning these are the waters the astrologers saw and misunderstood. They saw that Israel's savior would be struck through water, so פרעה said, 'Throw every baby boy into the river.' They did not know he would be struck over the waters of מריבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third and last person on the list: פרעה's astrologers. It uses a teaching of רבי חמא ברבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word הֵמָּה ('these are') in the פסוק is read as pointing to the waters the astrologers had seen. They read 'struck through water' as drowning, so they had the boys thrown into the river. Really it meant משה would be punished because of what happened at מי מריבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Astrologers, people who read the stars
The waters of מריבה, where משה hit the rock

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'struck through water' did not mean משה would drown. It meant he would be punished because of the water incident at מריבה.

phrases.english: The astrologers of Pharaoh,
as Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is meant by what is written: "These are the waters of Merivah"?
These are the waters that Pharaoh's astrologers saw, and they made a mistake.
They saw that the savior of Israel
would be struck through water,
so he said: "Every son that is born,
you shall throw into the river."
But they did not know
that he would be struck over the matter of the waters of Merivah.

steps.whatToRemember: All three people on the list saw a true sign but misread who or what it was about: נבט, אחיתופל, and פרעה's astrologers.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטַגְנִינֵי פַּרְעֹה, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final item on the list from step 13. This closes the side discussion about misread signs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The astrologers' vision of the savior being struck through water referred to מי מריבה, not to drowning.

steps.title: Asking for the source that ירבעם loses עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to ירבעם and asks how we know he has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that ירבעם does not come to עולם הבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list of kings and asks for a source that ירבעם loses עולם הבא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated that ירבעם has no share in עולם הבא, but it gave no source. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק to support that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know
that he does not come to the World to Come?
phrases.notes: 'He' is ירבעם, the first king listed in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא לַן דְּלָא אָתֵי לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the misread-signs topic and goes back to ירבעם from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that ירבעם loses his share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The פסוק shows ירבעם is destroyed in both worlds
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says ירבעם's house would be 'eradicated' and 'destroyed.' The first word means this world, and the second means עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the sin brought ירבעם's house 'to eradicate and to destroy from the face of the earth.' 'To eradicate' means in this world, and 'to destroy' means in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a פסוק and explaining its two verbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two words for destruction, so the גמרא gives each one its own meaning. One describes punishment in this world, and the other describes losing עולם הבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the פסוק source for the משנה's statement about the first king on its list.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And it was through this matter
a sin for the house of Jeroboam,
and to eradicate it and to destroy it
from off the face of the earth."
"To eradicate" means in this world,
"and to destroy" means for the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיְהִי בַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה לְחַטַּאת בֵּית יָרׇבְעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The double language 'eradicate' and 'destroy' in מלכים א 13:34 covers both this world and עולם הבא.

steps.title: Why ירבעם rose to kingship and why he was punished
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says ירבעם became king because he rebuked שלמה. He was punished because he did it in public. He accused שלמה of closing the wall's openings that דוד had made for the pilgrims.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why did ירבעם earn the kingship? Because he rebuked שלמה. Why was he punished? Because he rebuked him in public. The פסוק says he 'lifted his hand against the king' over שלמה's building the מלוא and closing the breach of עיר דוד. ירבעם told him: 'Your father דוד made openings in the wall so Israel could come up for the רגל, and you closed them to make forced labor for פרעה's daughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains ירבעם's rise and fall. Both came from the same act, his rebuke of שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rebuking a sinner was a merit, and it earned ירבעם the throne. But he did it in front of everyone and embarrassed the king, so he was punished. The פסוק about 'lifting his hand' over the wall repairs is read as describing that public rebuke.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebuked, told someone what he did wrong
In public, in front of many people

steps.whatToRemember: The same act can bring reward and punishment. Rebuking was right, but humiliating the king in public was wrong.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For what reason did Jeroboam earn the kingship?
Because he rebuked Solomon.
And for what reason was he punished?
Because he rebuked him in public,
as it is said: "And this was the matter
in which he lifted his hand against the king:
Solomon built the Millo,

phrases.aramaic: סָגַר אֶת פֶּרֶץ עִיר דָּוִד אָבִיו״.
phrases.english: and closed the breach of the city of David his father."
He said to him:
David your father made openings in the wall
so that Israel could come up for the festival,
and you closed them up
in order to make forced labor for the daughter of Pharaoh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה זָכָה יָרׇבְעָם לַמַּלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps discussing ירבעם after the proof that he loses עולם הבא, now explaining his rise and his punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם earned the kingship by rebuking שלמה, but he was punished for doing it publicly.

steps.title: What does 'he raised a hand against the king' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means when it says ירבעם 'raised a hand against the king.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'and this is why he raised a hand against the king'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly ירבעם did that the פסוק calls 'raising a hand' against שלמה. It is setting up רב נחמן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said ירבעם rebuked שלמה in public. Now the גמרא wants to know what 'raising a hand' means, since he did not actually hit the king.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a hand, meaning rebelled or acted against someone

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'and this is why he raised a hand against the king'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי ״וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר הֵרִים יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the same פסוק about ירבעם and שלמה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What act is meant by 'raising a hand' against the king

steps.title: He took off his תפילין in front of שלמה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that ירבעם removed his תפילין in front of the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It means he took off his תפילין in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains that 'raising a hand' was a disrespectful act: ירבעם took off his תפילין in front of שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No real hand was raised. Doing this in front of the king was treated as rebellion, because it showed he did not respect שלמה as his superior.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, worn on the head and arm

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
That he removed his tefillin in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: שֶׁחָלַץ תְּפִילָּיו בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Raising a hand' means ירבעם removed his תפילין in front of שלמה, a sign of disrespect

steps.title: ירבעם's arrogance drove him out of עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says ירבעם's arrogance cost him עולם הבא. He brings the פסוק where ירבעם worries that the people will go back to רחבעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The arrogance in ירבעם drove him out of the world, as it says: 'And ירבעם said in his heart: Now the kingdom will go back to the house of דוד. If this people goes up to bring sacrifices in the house of ה׳ in ירושלים, the people's heart will turn back to their master, to רחבעם king of יהודה, and they will kill me and go back to רחבעם king of יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a new statement: ירבעם's arrogance is what made him lose עולם הבא. He quotes the פסוק that shows ירבעם's worried thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The root of ירבעם's downfall was pride and fear of losing his crown. The פסוק shows him worrying that if the people went to ירושלים for the holidays, they would leave him for רחבעם. The next step explains why he thought this.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The arrogance that was in Jeroboam
drove him out of the world,
phrases.notes: He means עולם הבא. This ties back to step 18.

phrases.english: as it is said:
'And Jeroboam said in his heart:
Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.
If this people goes up
to offer sacrifices in the House of ה׳ in Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁב לֵב הָעָם הַזֶּה אֶל אֲדֹנֵיהֶם
phrases.english: the heart of this people will turn back to their master,
to Rehoboam, king of Judah,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרָגֻנִי וְשָׁבוּ אֶל רְחַבְעָם מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה״.
phrases.english: and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam, king of Judah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ בְּיָרׇבְעָם טְרָדַתּוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement of רב נחמן, giving the deeper cause of ירבעם's loss of עולם הבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם's arrogance and fear for his throne caused him to lose עולם הבא

steps.title: ירבעם's fear: only kings of יהודה may sit in the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: ירבעם reasons that only kings of יהודה may sit in the עזרה. If he stands while רחבעם sits, he looks like a servant. If he sits, he is a rebel.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירבעם said: We have a tradition that no one may sit in the עזרה except kings of the house of יהודה. When people see רחבעם sitting and me standing, they will think: this one is the king and that one is the servant. And if I sit, I am a rebel against the kingdom, and they will kill me and follow him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ירבעם feared the people would kill him: in the בית המקדש he would look smaller than רחבעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in the reason behind ירבעם's words in the פסוק. Either choice was bad for him. Standing makes him look like a servant, and sitting makes him a rebel. His pride could not accept either one.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (we learned it)
Sitting in the עזרה, the Temple courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: This is ירבעם's own reasoning, not the גמרא speaking. The words 'I' and 'me' refer to ירבעם.

phrases.english: He said: We have a tradition
that there is no sitting in the Temple courtyard
except for kings of the house of Judah alone.
Once they see Rehoboam sitting
and me standing,
they will think: This one is the king and that one is the servant.
And if I sit, I am a rebel against the kingdom,
and they will kill me and follow him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: גְּמִירִי דְּאֵין יְשִׁיבָה בַּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind ירבעם's fear in the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם feared the rule that only kings of יהודה may sit in the עזרה would make him look like רחבעם's servant

steps.title: So ירבעם made two golden calves
steps.stepSummary: Right away, ירבעם took counsel and made two golden calves, one in בית אל and one in דן, so the people would not go up to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately: 'The king took counsel and made two golden calves. He said to them: It is too much for you to go up to ירושלים. Here are your gods, ישראל, who brought you up from the land of מצרים. And he put one in בית אל and the other he put in דן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the result of ירבעם's fear. He set up golden calves so the people would stop going to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'immediately' links his prideful worry directly to the sin. To protect his crown, he created a different place of worship. This is how his arrogance led to idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: It is too much for you
A town in the south of ירבעם's kingdom

steps.whatToRemember: ירבעם's arrogance led him to fear losing his throne. That fear led him to make the golden calves.

phrases.english: Immediately: 'And the king took counsel
and made two calves of gold,

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם רַב לָכֶם מֵעֲלוֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַים
phrases.english: and said to them: It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem;
here are your gods, Israel,
who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
And he placed the one in Beit El,
and the other he put in Dan.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד ״וַיִּוָּעַץ הַמֶּלֶךְ וַיַּעַשׂ שְׁנֵי עֶגְלֵי זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the action that came from ירבעם's reasoning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of his fear, ירבעם immediately made two golden calves to keep the people from ירושלים

steps.title: What does 'took counsel' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'ויועץ' (took counsel) in the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'took counsel'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on one word from the פסוק it just quoted. It is setting up רבי יהודה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ירבעם 'took counsel' but does not say with whom or how. The גמרא wants to know how he got advisors to support such a terrible plan.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'and he took counsel'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וַיִּוָּעַץ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק quoted in step 24
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How and with whom ירבעם took counsel

steps.title: He seated a wicked man next to a righteous man
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that ירבעם seated each righteous advisor next to a wicked one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: He seated a wicked man next to a righteous man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers that ירבעם arranged his advisors so that a wicked person sat beside each righteous person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This was a trick. The wicked advisor would be there to influence the righteous one sitting next to him. The next step shows how it worked.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
That he seated a wicked man next to a righteous man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: שֶׁהוֹשִׁיב רָשָׁע אֵצֶל צַדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Took counsel' means ירבעם seated wicked advisors beside righteous ones in order to manipulate them

steps.title: ירבעם tricks the elders step by step
steps.stepSummary: ירבעם got the elders to keep saying 'yes,' then asked about idol worship. When a righteous man refused, the wicked man beside him said ירבעם was only testing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Will you sign on to everything I do? They said: Yes. He said: I want to be king. They said: Yes. Will you do everything I tell you? They said: Yes. Even to worship idols? The righteous man said: Heaven forbid! The wicked man said to the righteous man: Do you really think a man like ירבעם would worship idols? He only wants to test them, to see if they will accept his word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story of how the trick worked. ירבעם got many 'yeses' first. Then the wicked man calmed the righteous man's objection to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירבעם built up agreement with easy questions before asking the big one. When the righteous man refused, the wicked man beside him said it was only a loyalty test. This is exactly why the seating plan from step 26 mattered.
steps.whatToRemember: ירבעם used pressure and trickery. He got the elders to agree to small things first, and he placed wicked men beside the righteous ones to calm their objections.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: חָתְמִיתוּ עַל כֹּל דְּעָבֵידְנָא?
phrases.english: He said to them: Will you sign on to everything I do?
They said to him: Yes.
He said to them: I want to be king.
They said to him: Yes.
Will you do everything I tell you?
They said to him: Yes.
Even to worship idols?
A righteous man said to him: Heaven forbid!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָשָׁע לְצַדִּיק: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
phrases.english: The wicked man said to the righteous man: Does it enter your mind
that a man like Jeroboam would worship idols?
Rather, he only wants to test them,
to see if you will accept his word.
phrases.notes: The wording jumps from 'them' to 'you.' It means everyone sitting there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: חָתְמִיתוּ עַל כֹּל דְּעָבֵידְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story that shows how the seating trick from step 26 worked
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם won the elders' agreement through a chain of 'yes' answers, with wicked men talking the righteous out of objecting to idol worship
